questions.question: The study of the structure of the body is called:
questions.explanation:
Anatomy is the branch of science that deals with the structure of the body and the relationships between its parts. It comes from the Greek words ana (up) and tomia (cutting), reflecting its origins in dissection.

• Physiology studies how body parts function.
• Histology studies tissues at the microscopic level.
• Pathology studies disease and its effects on structure and function.

questions.question: Which branch of study deals with tissues at the microscopic level?
questions.explanation:
Histology (microscopic anatomy) is the study of the microscopic structure of tissues. It involves preparing thin slices of tissue, staining them, and examining them under a microscope.

• Gross anatomy deals with structures visible to the naked eye.
• Physiology studies function.
• Surface anatomy studies external body features.

questions.question: Physiology is best defined as the study of:
options: The size, shape and position of organs
questions.explanation:
Physiology is the study of the functions of the body and its parts — how organs, tissues, and cells carry out their activities and work together to maintain life.

• Size, shape, and position belong to anatomy.
• Tissues under a microscope belong to histology.
• Naming body regions belongs to anatomical terminology.

questions.question: Gross anatomy deals with structures that are:
options: Seen only with an electron microscope
questions.explanation: Gross (macroscopic) anatomy studies structures that are large enough to be seen with the naked eye, such as organs, bones, and muscles. It contrasts with microscopic anatomy (histology), which requires a microscope.

questions.question: The term \anterior\ means:
options: Towards the back of the body
questions.explanation:
In anatomical terminology, anterior means towards the front of the body. For example, the sternum (breastbone) is anterior to the vertebral column.

• Towards the head = superior (cranial).
• Towards the feet = inferior (caudal).
• Towards the back = posterior (dorsal).

questions.question: Which term is the opposite of \superior\?
questions.explanation:
Superior means towards the head (upper), while inferior means towards the feet (lower). They are opposite directional terms.

• Posterior is opposite anterior.
• Medial is opposite lateral.
• Anterior is opposite posterior, not superior.

questions.question: Which system receives information and coordinates the body's responses?
questions.explanation:
The nervous system is the body's primary control and communication system. It receives sensory information, processes it, and coordinates rapid responses through electrical impulses and chemical signals.

• Integumentary system protects the body.
• Reproductive system produces gametes.
• Cardiovascular system transports substances.

questions.question: Which plane divides the body into left and right portions?
questions.explanation:
A sagittal plane is a vertical plane that divides the body into left and right portions. If it passes exactly through the midline, it is a midsagittal plane.

• Coronal (frontal) plane divides front and back.
• Transverse (horizontal) plane divides upper and lower.

questions.question: The coronal (frontal) plane divides the body into:
options: Equal halves along the midline only
questions.explanation:
The coronal (frontal) plane is a vertical plane that divides the body into anterior (front) and posterior (back) portions.

• Sagittal divides left and right.
• Transverse divides upper and lower.

questions.question: The transverse (horizontal) plane divides the body into:
options: Equal right and left halves through the midline
questions.explanation:
The transverse (horizontal) plane divides the body into upper (superior) and lower (inferior) portions.

• Coronal divides front and back.
• Sagittal divides left and right.

questions.question: A midsagittal plane divides the body into:
questions.explanation:
A midsagittal plane is a sagittal plane that passes exactly through the midline of the body, dividing it into equal left and right halves.

• A parasagittal plane would divide it into unequal portions.
• Coronal and transverse planes divide differently.

questions.question: A parasagittal plane divides the body into:
options: Upper and lower portions of the body
questions.explanation:
A parasagittal plane is any sagittal plane that does not pass through the midline, so it divides the body into unequal left and right portions.

• Midsagittal gives equal halves.
• Coronal gives front/back.
• Transverse gives upper/lower.

questions.question: The smallest unit of an element is the:
questions.explanation:
An atom is the smallest unit of an element that retains the properties of that element. Atoms combine to form molecules.

• Organelles are structures inside cells.
• Molecules are groups of atoms bonded together.
• Tissues are groups of similar cells.

questions.question: Which level of organization lies immediately between tissue and organ system?
questions.explanation:
The levels of structural organization from simplest to most complex are: atom → molecule → organelle → cell → tissue → organ → organ system → organism.

Therefore, between tissue and organ system lies the organ.

questions.question: The basic structural and functional unit of the living body is the:
questions.explanation:
The cell is the basic structural and functional unit of all living organisms. It is the smallest unit that can carry out all life processes.

• Tissues are groups of cells.
• Organs are made of tissues.
• Molecules are chemical structures.

questions.question: A specialized structure found inside a cell is called a(n):
questions.explanation:
An organelle is a specialized structure within a cell that performs a specific function (e.g., mitochondrion, nucleus, ribosome).

• Tissues are groups of cells.
• Molecules are chemical compounds.
• Organ systems are groups of organs.

questions.question: A group of similar cells working together is called a:
questions.explanation: A tissue is a group of similar cells that work together to perform a specific function. The four main tissue types are epithelial, connective, muscle, and nervous tissue.

questions.question: An organ is made up of:
questions.explanation: An organ is composed of two or more different tissue types that work together to perform a specific function. For example, the stomach contains epithelial, connective, muscle, and nervous tissues.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an organ system?
questions.explanation:
An organ system is a group of organs that work together to perform major functions. The urinary system (kidneys, ureters, bladder, urethra) is an organ system.

• Cardiac muscle cell is a cell.
• Mitochondrion is an organelle.
• Connective tissue is a tissue.

questions.question: All the organ systems working together make up a(n):
questions.explanation: The highest level of structural organization is the organism, which consists of all the organ systems working together to maintain life.

questions.question: The four major tissue types of the body are:
questions.explanation: The four primary tissue types are epithelial, connective, muscle, and nervous tissue. Skeletal, cardiac, and adipose are subtypes or examples within these categories, not major types.

questions.question: The ability of the body to detect and respond to changes is called:
questions.explanation: Responsiveness (irritability) is the ability to detect changes in the internal or external environment and respond appropriately. It is a key characteristic of living organisms.

questions.question: The process by which cells become specialized for particular functions is:
questions.explanation: Differentiation is the process by which unspecialized cells (stem cells) develop into specialized cells with specific structures and functions.

questions.question: The production of new cells or offspring is called:
questions.explanation: Reproduction is the process by which organisms produce new cells or offspring. At the cellular level, it involves cell division; at the organism level, it ensures continuation of the species.

questions.question: The removal of waste products from the body is known as:
questions.explanation: Excretion is the process of removing metabolic wastes (e.g., carbon dioxide, urea) from the body. It is essential for maintaining homeostasis.

questions.question: Which structures belong to the integumentary system?
questions.explanation: The integumentary system consists of the skin, hair, nails, and various glands (sweat, sebaceous). It protects the body, regulates temperature, and provides sensation.

questions.question: Which system is made up of glands and hormones, and controls growth, metabolism and reproduction?
options: Nerve cells and the spinal cord
questions.explanation: The endocrine system consists of glands that secrete hormones, which regulate growth, metabolism, reproduction, and many other body functions.

questions.question: Which system transports oxygen, nutrients and waste through the body?
questions.explanation: The cardiovascular system (heart, blood vessels, blood) transports oxygen, nutrients, hormones, and waste products throughout the body.

questions.question: Which function belongs to the urinary system?
options: Absorption of nutrients from digested food
questions.explanation: The urinary system removes metabolic wastes (e.g., urea) and regulates fluid, electrolyte, and acid-base balance by producing urine.

questions.question: The production of gametes and the continuation of the species is the function of the:
questions.explanation: The reproductive system produces gametes (sperm and ova) and is responsible for the continuation of the species through sexual reproduction.

questions.question: Which of the following are organs of special senses?
questions.explanation: The organs of special senses include the eyes (vision), ears (hearing and balance), nose (smell), and tongue (taste). They contain specialized receptors for these senses.
